name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 7, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission
Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m., on February 7, 2011, at
200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 2, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator Government Code Section 54956.8. The
  unimproved real property commonly referred to as “Site C” located on City-owned
  land directly adjacent to and southeasterly of the City’s Animal Service Center off
  Center Drive, and easterly of Saddleback College (Assessor Parcel No. 740-112-03).

City Council Minutes  1  February 7, 2011
   City/CDA Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager/CDA Executive Director,
  Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager, Charles Wilson, Director of Community
  Development, James Williams, Economic Advisor, Celeste Brady, CDA Counsel,
  and William Curley, III, City Attorney. Under negotiation and discussion: City
  Council and CDA will provide direction regarding price and terms for soliciting
  proposals for disposition and development of the approximate 37-acre Site C, either
  or both the approximate 8.5-acre sub-parcel zoned RPD-30A for affordable housing
  development and the approximate 28.5 acre sub-parcel zoned Recreation.

RECESS

At the hour of 5:14 p.m., Mayor Leckness declared a recess to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Mayor Pro Tem Ury was
absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council provided direction to staff regarding
their intent to limit discussion to the 8.5 acre site for affordable housing purposes. Staff will
return to the City Council with a draft RFP and, once approved by the Council, the matter will be
discussed in a public forum.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adoptable Pets of the Month

  Mayor Leckness highlighted four animals available for adoption at the Mission Viejo
  Animal Services Center.

P2.  Recognize the 2010 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Leckness presented plaques to Budget and Research Manager Nancy Livingston,
  City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; Deputy Sheriff II Robert Franz, Orange
  County Sheriff’s Department Employee of the Year; and Firefighter Chuck Hawkins,
  Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year.

P3.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Leckness and the Marine Adoption Committee presented certificates of
  commendation to Sergeant George M. Martinez and Private First Class Jordan M.
  O’Donoghue. Michelle Clark presented the Marines with tickets to a Lakers game,
  courtesy of Waste Management.

City Council Minutes  2  February 7, 2011
 P4.  Presentation by Moulton Niguel Water District on the new Water-Budget-Based
  Rate Structure

  The City Council received a presentation from Moulton Niguel Water District Board
  Member Richard Fiore, General Manager Dr. Robert Gumerman, and Director of
  Customer Service Charles Roy.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Mickey Schulte, M.V.: announced that the Lions Club celebrates Flag Day in February by
presenting local 2nd graders with a miniature American flag and a flag data sheet and he provided
one for each City Council Member.

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that Mission Viejo is a well-planned community and there is a valid
perception that spending is out of control. In light of the present economic situation, he feels that
the solution to a new dog park or tennis center remodel is to pass the costs along to the residents
who would use the facilities.

Jim and Robin Sickles: thanked the Mayor and City Council for adjourning tonight’s meeting in
memory of their son, Robert Sickles.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: reminded residents of the Tee it Up Fore Marines golf tournament on
March 25, 2011, at the Marine Memorial Golf Course in Camp Pendleton.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 6, and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  3  February 7, 2011
   Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 17, 2011, as
  presented.

4.  Check Register dated January 7, 2011, in the amount of $699,438.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated January 14, 2011, in the amount of $810,972.19

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Reduction in Community Development Agency (CDA) Outstanding Loan Balance

  (1) Adopted Resolution 11-09 Amending the FY 2010-11 Budget to Reflect a Payment
  of General Fund Loans by the Community Development Agency (CDA), and (2) adopted
  CDA Resolution 11-02 Amending the FY 2010-11 Budget to Reflect a Payment of
  General Fund Loans.

9.  Federal-Aid Safe-Route-To-School Project

  Adopted Resolution 11-10 Approving and Authorizing Execution of Program
  Supplement No. N021 to Administering Agency-State Agreement No. 12-5451R for
  Federal-Aid Projects between the State Department of Transportation and the City of
  Mission Viejo.

10.  American Recovery & Reinvestment Act of 2009 (ARRA)-Energy Efficient Light
  Fixtures and Bulb Replacements at the Norman P. Murray Center, Civic Center
  and City Traffic Signals (CIP 320)

  Approved the plans and bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for the
  replacement of fixtures and lights at the Civic Center and Community Center and lights at
  City traffic signals.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Summary of FY 2010-11 Budget Amendments To Date

City Council Minutes  4  February 7, 2011
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht wondered if repayment of the city's loan was an attempt to
  protect redevelopment funds from the State and she asked how strong the CDA is,
  without the city having to loan it money for its operations and debt.

  Mr. Bornstein responded that it is common for the city to loan money to the CDA at the
  end of each fiscal year.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

6.  Check Register dated January 21, 2011, in the amount of $1,824,915.86

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the payment to Mayer, Hoffman and McCann
  as listed on page 14 of the staff report. She asked if the public notice has been published
  in the newspaper.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein announced
  that the notice was published in the Saddleback Valley News before the end of the 2010
  calendar year.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

8.  Consent to Transfer Agreement between Joanna Bock, Owner/CFO of Medix
  Ambulance Service (the Transferor) and Michael Dimas, Owner/CEO of Medix
  Ambulance Service (the Transferee) to transfer the ownership of Transferor’s
  interest in the stock of Medix Ambulance Service

City Council Minutes  5  February 7, 2011
   Council Member Reardon noted that she spoke to Mr. Dimas and to City Attorney Curley
  to request that a "no dissolution related challenge" be added to the contract in order to
  protect the city.

  City Attorney Curley announced that he will add a clause to indemnify the city so the
  Dimas’ marital issues will not impact the agreement.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve the Consent to Transfer Agreement (as amended) between Joanna Bock,
  Owner/CFO of Medix Ambulance Service (Transferor) and Michael Dimas, Owner/CEO
  for Medix Ambulance Service (Transferee) to transfer the ownership of Transferor’s
  interest in the stock of Medix Ambulance Service, Inc. to Transferee.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

11.  South Orange County Watershed Management Area Executive Committee

  Mayor Leckness appointed Council Member Reardon as the City’s representative and
  Council Member Schlicht as alternate to the South Orange County Watershed
  Management Area Executive Committee.

  Mayor Leckness announced that he will also make an adjustment to the CUSD ad hoc
  committee. He would like to participate on that committee and Council Member Reardon
  has agreed to step aside so he can serve on the ad hoc.

12.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

13.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness presented the report.

14.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness had no report at this time.

15.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

City Council Minutes  6  February 7, 2011
   Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg announced that he will distribute an RFP for lease of the Thomas R.
Potocki Conference Center. He reminded the Council that last year, they directed staff to develop
an RFP and the document will now wind its way through the Community Services Commission
and will ultimately come back to the Council for consideration.

Mr. Wilberg also noted that the City's 2010 Annual Report is available on the web site and a
limited number of copies have been printed for distribution at City facilities.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley thanked Karen Hamman and city staff for putting together the 2010
Annual Report. She takes a lot of pride as she reads the positive news from the City’s budget to
its safest city ranking. There are good facts and figures in the report and she encouraged
residents to take a look on-line or to obtain a copy at one of the City’s facilities. Council
Member Kelley announced that she attended the ribbon cutting and grand opening for Hand and
Stone Massage in Plaza del Lago and she was pleased and proud to visit Mission Viejo High
School’s national college signing day where a number of talented MVHS athletes were awarded
scholarships by various colleges. Today, she also attended career day at La Paz Intermediate
School. She reminded residents that they host a newspaper drive every Friday from 7:30 a.m. to
8:30 a.m. in the upper parking lot. The school raises about $1,000 every week and they are
always seeking additional donations. Council Member Kelley announced that she is a member
of the Saddleback College Foundation and they held their annual fundraiser this past week.
College students prepared the food and Capistrano Valley High School students handled the
serving and set up; she noted that it was another great event. Council Member Kelley
congratulated Employees of the Year Nancy Livingston, Sheriff’s Deputy Robert Franz and
Firefighter Chuck Hawkins and she expressed her thanks to these public servants. She also
recognized Snuffy Brown, a member of the Marine Adoption Committee, and the City’s first
Hometown Veteran Hero. Council Member Kelley stated that it was wonderful to see Snuffy
here with the young Marines that were honored this evening and it provided a great visual picture

City Council Minutes  7  February 7, 2011
 of our American Heroes. In conclusion, Council Member Kelley announced that the Community
of Character word for the month of February is unity.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that she too attended the Mission Viejo High School Letter
of Intent Ceremony. She congratulated Mayor Leckness on his key note address which was
pertinent and relevant to the young people listening. She noted that there were 25 athletes
honored that day and there were many touching stories to be heard. Students recognized were:

  Mariah Helmer  San Diego State University  Soccer
  Erik Macke  St. Mary's College  Soccer
  Christian Gonzalez  Cal State Northridge  Soccer
  Chris Britt  West Pointe  Soccer
  Alison McKibbon  Humboldt State University  Softball
  Nicole Byron  University of Maine  Softball
  Amanda Fernandez  Boston University  Softball
  Tre Madden  USC  Football
  Ryan Muno  San Diego State  Baseball
  Austin Saenz  Cal State Fullerton  Baseball
  Willie Kuhl  Cal State Fullerton  Baseball
  Ryan Raslowsky  Cal State Northridge  Baseball
  Matt Marsh  UC Santa Barbara  Volleyball
  Danielle White  Georgetown University  Volleyball
  Jillian Meyers  University of Delaware  Volleyball
  Ver'Leea Hardaway  Washington State  Volleyball
  Megan Armes  St. Mary's College  Lacrosse
  Isaac Nielsen  Brigham Young University  Basketball
  Erin Butler  University of Arizona  Basketball
  Sasha Westberg  Navy  Swimming
  Mitch Melugin  Northern Arizona University  Football
  Erika Schaefer  University of Oregon  Acrobatics/Tumbling
  Christine Rommel  San Jose State University  Diving
  Michael Schmall  University of Pennsylvania  Football
  Ethan DeSilva  Yale  Football
  Dallas Kessman  Announcement is pending  Football
  Bryan Keller  Announcement is pending  Football

Council Member Reardon, along with Mayor Leckness, attended the School to Watch
celebration at La Paz Intermediate. She was impressed with the Principal, Jean Carroll, who has
turned the school around and has gained the teachers’ strong support. Council Member Reardon
also expressed her admiration for the school’s Where Everyone Belongs (WEB) program. 8th
graders get together and welcome the 7th graders during the first month of school and she heard
from parents whose children actually enjoy the middle school transition as a result of this
program. Council Member Reardon reported on her young friend, Cade, who had two brain

City Council Minutes  8  February 7, 2011
 surgeries in less than a month. While he has been released from CHOC hospital in Orange and is
making vast improvements, she asked everyone to continue thinking about and praying for Cade.
Council Member Reardon announced that she is a member of the YMCA Board of Directors and
they are organizing a Partners Campaign which is a fundraiser for childcare and memberships
scholarships. Last year, the YMCA gave $20,000 more in scholarships than they were able to
secure in donations.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that she is so happy to hear about Council Member Reardon’s
friend Cade; it is proof that prayers are being answered. She reminded residents that the City
will hold its regular Council Meeting on Presidents Day, Monday, January 21. She also
congratulated the employee of the year recipients and stated that folks like these make the
difference and keep us safe and secure. Council Member Schlicht summarized her attendance at
recent events: the Lake Forest City Council Meeting on January 18, 2011, when they became the
14th Orange County city to approve the motto “In God We Trust” for display in their city hall;
on January 20, she attended the Saddleback Valley Unified School District Board meeting as
Mission Viejo High School football coach Bob Johnson was acknowledged for 37 years in the
District; on January 27 she attended the OCCOG Board Meeting when the Board Members voted
to fill an empty seat for District 13. Council Member Schlicht congratulated the Mission Viejo
High School student athletes who were honored at the National Letter of Intent signing day. She
noted that these young people will need to learn how to be successful college students by
balancing their academics and sports and to also have a social life. She further announced that
on Thursday Feb 3, she reviewed and commented in favor of the Desert Recreation District’s
application for membership in the Joint Powers Insurance Authority. Last Friday she attended
the Saddleback College Gaucho double-header basketball games and she announced that this
Wednesday is the last opportunity to see the Gauchos play a home game in the regular season.
Council Member Schlicht noted that Supervisor Pat Bates, in her State of the County address,
expressed her concerns about the financial challenges ahead and she stated that the County is one
of the first in the State to take on the battle of pension reform. Council Member Schlicht also
announced that she will meet with developers on February 17 to discuss a pending housing
project. She thanked Assistant City Manager and Director of Administrative Services Irwin
Bornstein for his many years of service and dedication to the City of Mission Viejo and she
congratulated him on his upcoming retirement. In conclusion, Council Member Schlicht shared
a quote from President Reagan’s 1984 State of the Union address, in honor of his 100th birthday:
“After all our struggles to restore America, to revive confidence in our country, hope for our
future, after all our hard-won victories earned through the patience and courage of every citizen,
we cannot, must not, and will not turn back. We will finish our job. How could we do less?
We're Americans.”

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness announced that he is not embarrassed to admit that he enjoyed a facial massage
while attending the grand opening of the Hand and Stone spa in Mission Viejo. He also
expressed his appreciation to Director of Public Services Keith Rattay for the unbelievable

City Council Minutes  9  February 7, 2011
 transformation of the City Council Chamber for Saturday’s KSBR radio show. The room looked
like the Tonight Show stage and it was a fantastic, first class program. Mr. Leckness announced
that he enjoyed talking with residents and staff at his “Meet the Mayor” event and he will host
these get-togethers at a different location each month while he is Mayor.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour or 8:19 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Robert Allen Sickles to Monday, February
21, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 21, 2011

City Council Minutes  10  February 7, 2011
